summary: Valeria Gazizova specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She prepared her master's thesis at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kværne (attested 2009).

Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. Educated at Occidental College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale University, he taught at Princeton, Southern Methodist University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Stanford University.

Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army from 1817 to 1835 and later was president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1846).

Sinologist Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev (1881–1951) studied at St. Petersburg University and under Édouard Chavannes. His main career included positions at Saint Petersburg State University (~1910–1951), the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1918–1951), and the National Library of Russia (1924–1926).

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev (1818–1900) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Kazan Federal University under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski, later holding professorships at Kazan and Saint Petersburg State University, and a post at the Imperial Academy of Sciences.

Vasily Seseman (1884–1963) was a philosopher who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1903–1909). He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1915–1918), Vytautas Magnus University (~1923–1940), and Vilnius University (~1940–1950).

Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale (1901–1996) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. After completing his PhD at the University of Bonn by 1930, he held academic positions at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi (attested 1966).

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi (1893–1985) was an Indology and archaeology scholar educated at Deccan College and the University of Mumbai. He served as Principal at Morris College and Vidarbha Mahavidyalaya, and was a professor at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (1957–1966).

Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala (1904–1967) was an Indology and archaeology scholar educated at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He held posts at the Government Museum in Mathura, the State Museum in Lucknow, the ASI, and Banaras Hindu University.

Vasudha Dalmia (born 1947) works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Delhi, Cologne, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Heidelberg, she held positions at Tübingen, JNU, the University of California, Berkeley (~1998–2012), Free University of Berlin, and Yale University.

Vasudha Narayanan (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the universities of Madras, Mumbai, and Harvard. She was appointed Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida (~1982) and served as president of the AAR.

Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi (born 1973) works in Indology and philosophy. After studying under Manikya Shastri and Martanda Dikshit, he held posts at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha, the French Institute of Pondicherry, Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Rajasthan Sanskrit University, and Karnataka Samskrit University.

Velcheru Narayana Rao (born 1933) is an Indologist educated at Sir C.R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University. He served as Associate Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971) and held visiting professorships at Chicago and Emory.

Vempati Kutumba Sastry (born 1950) is an Indology scholar who served as Vice-Chancellor of the Central Sanskrit University (2003–2008) and president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~2006–2018).
Ven. Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhante Dhammasakkaro and earned a PhD from The University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007–2009).

Verity Harte (born 1968) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge. She held fellowships at St Edmund's and St Hilda's, taught at King's College London (~1999–2005), and became a professor of Philosophy and Classics at Yale in 2006.

Verrier Elwin (1902–1964) was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Dean Close School and Merton College (~1921–1925). He served as the first deputy director of the Anthropological Survey of India from around 1946 to 1949.

Vesna Wallace (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After doctoral studies at UC Berkeley, she held posts at UC Berkeley, the University of Oxford as Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies (until 2010), and the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Victor B. Lieberman (born 1945) is a historian who earned his BA at Yale and his PhD at SOAS University of London. In 1984, he became Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan (born 1945) is a Tibetology scholar who was a graduate student at the University of Chicago. He served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia (attested 2005).
